subject: Pilot MAP: performance acceptance gates & benchmarking plan

Subject: Pilot MAP: performance acceptance gates & benchmarking plan

Hi Samantha and Tom —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we want to lock down a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on validating performance SLOs for your primary flows before you commit to Dedicated capacity. I attached a first-pass MAP spreadsheet that lays out milestones and acceptance gates.

Goal for this thread: agree scope for the benchmarking phase (workload shape, TTFT targets, throughput/concurrency expectations), define clear success criteria, and confirm dates so we can align infra and test harness.

Proposed high-level benchmarking scope (quick bullet):
- Workloads: 3 representative flows (patient intake free-text, eligibility bot, document summarization)
- TTFT: 95th percentile end-to-end first-token-times for conversational flows
- Throughput: sustained token/sec at peak concurrency
- Concurrency: default plan: 50 parallel chat sessions, scale test to 200 sessions for burst profile
- Acceptance gates: pass/fail per flow + aggregate latency budget + regex/quality check on outputs

Can you confirm sample QPS/concurrency you expect in production, and any additional flows we should include? If that looks OK I’ll loop in Karthik to propose the exact test harness, datasets, and success criteria cells in the MAP.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Pilot MAP: performance acceptance gates & benchmarking plan

Thanks Ben — this is exactly the structure we wanted. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic profile: steady-state for the pilot is ~30 active sessions (chat-like patient support) with peak bursts up to ~120 over a 5-min window. Token distribution skews short (median 20 tokens per user-turn) but we have occasional long summarization requests (~1.5k tokens).
2) Key flows: prioritize (a) triage chat (low-latency), (b) eligibility assistant (medium context, up to 512 tokens), (c) clinical note summarization (high context, long outputs).
3) Success criteria we want to see in MAP before moving to Dedicated:
   - TTFT (first response from model) <= 600ms at 95th for triage chat
   - Sustained throughput: support 30 sessions with 1.5 RPS per session for triage chat with p95 latency <= 800ms
   - For summarization: average time-to-complete <= 6s for 1.5k token inputs at 95th
4) Compliance check: we will need evidence of request tracing and per-token billing breakdown for audit.

We can be flexible with dates but prefer to finish benchmarking and sign-off by the end of the quarter (target: Sep 10). Can Karthik or your test lead propose a concrete test plan with datasets and harness by Aug 28?

—Samantha

Thanks for the details — very helpful. Karthik will own the harness and will propose concrete test cases. Two quick notes:
- The 600ms p95 TTFT for triage chat is aggressive but achievable with the right model/quantization and colocated region; we’ll include a fallback plan (lighter quantized model) in the MAP if we see degradation during scale tests.
- For the long summarization runs, we’ll measure both TTFT and time-to-complete; acceptance will require meeting both latency and correctness checks (we’ll share suggested metrics for summarization quality).

I’ve added a target milestone to the MAP: Karthik delivers test plan + starter harness by Aug 28, Redwood runs benchmark Sep 1–3, joint review Sep 4–6, sign-off by Sep 10. If dates look tight we can shift the run window a week later.

Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@nimbushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood bench harness + acceptance gates (draft)

Hi Samantha — attaching the draft harness and proposed pass/fail thresholds. High level:

- Test harness: containerized runner (redwood_benchmark_harness.tar.gz) that can replay recorded session traces and synthetic traffic. It will capture TTFT (client-perceived first token), per-token latencies, total time-to-complete, error rates, and resource utilization (GPU utl, mem, kernel stalls).
- Datasets: we seeded three dataset buckets: triage_chat_samples (1k short dialogs), eligibility_queries (500 mid-length), long_summaries (120 long docs). Will share S3 links in the Drive folder.
- Success criteria (proposed):
   * Triage chat: p95 TTFT <= 650ms (with our default model); fallback model must keep p95 TTFT <= 800ms and error rate < 0.5%
   * Sustained throughput: 30 sessions * 1.5 RPS -> 45 RPS sustained; p95 latency <= 800ms
   * Burst profile: 120 sessions for 5-min window, aggregate p95 <= 1.2s
   * Summarization: p95 time-to-complete <= 6.5s with ROUGE-L >= 0.45 on sampled set
- Observability: we will emit trace IDs and per-request tokens so Nimbus can validate billing breakdowns.

Open items for you to confirm: exact sample docs for long_summaries (PHI redaction already done?), accept/reject on the ROUGE-L threshold, and whether OWASP or additional security scans are required for harness containers.

I attached the harness tar and a short runbook; happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the harness next week.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Park <samantha.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood bench harness + acceptance gates (draft)

Thanks Karthik — this looks good and very thorough. A few confirmations:

- PHI redaction: our security ops team has pre-redacted the long_summaries dataset; you can use the sample set in the Drive link.
- ROUGE-L: we can accept the 0.45 threshold for the pilot, provided you also include a manual spot-check step (5 random samples) in the runbook.
- Observability: trace IDs and per-token metadata suffice for our audit. We also need a short artifact that maps your per-token billing to our expected invoice line items (a one-pager is fine).
- Dates: Sep 1–3 run window is tight for us (engineering out this week). Can we run Sep 7–9 instead with joint review on Sep 10? That fits our internal cadence.

If that schedule works, we’ll mark the MAP milestone as: harness delivered Aug 28 (done), benchmark run Sep 7–9, joint review Sep 10, target sign-off Sep 10–12. I’ll drop a calendar invite for the Sep 10 review once Ben confirms.

—Samantha
